key_insight: A single camera representation can struggle to capture both a lens’s overall projection and its subtle variations. OmniRay proposes composite ray fields to represent this structure hierarchically for camera-agnostic monocular 3D reconstruction.
problem_solved: Monocular 3D models that assume pinhole cameras can distort geometry from fisheye and panoramic images. Existing camera-aware models use a single fixed basis to represent both global camera geometry and finer variations.
method: Represent camera geometry with per-pixel viewing rays rather than assuming a pinhole projection.
Use composite ray fields to model the hierarchy between overall camera projection and finer geometric variations. Detailed implementation is not available in the truncated abstract.
impact: The approach aims to make single-image 3D reconstruction more adaptable to different lens types, especially wide-angle imagery. The supplied excerpt does not include quantitative results.
visual_elements: Pinhole, fisheye, and panoramic images shown side by side to illustrate different projections.
A ray-field diagram showing viewing directions associated with image pixels.
A conceptual hierarchy separating overall camera projection from fine-scale variations.
A pipeline diagram: single image → composite ray field → reconstructed 3D geometry.
paper_title: OmniRay: Camera-Agnostic Monocular 3D Reconstruction with Composite Ray Fields
paper_authors: Namitha Guruprasad, Abhay Yadav, Cheng Peng, Rama Chellappa, Anand Bhattad
